thread:
deploy-bot: Progressive rollout started for service=runtime-inference image=redwood/inference:v2.4.0 canary=10% (strategy=progressive-release)
incident-bot: PAGER: Sev2 — increased 5xx rate on /v1/generate for prod-us-east-1. Alert: error-rate > 3% over 3m. Link: https://metrics.redwood.local/d/r/alerts
sara (oncall): seeing steady 503/504s, customers reporting slow responses. Rolling windows show latency spike coincident with canary start. Paging now. @raj can you triage? :rotating_light:
raj: on it. grabbing logs from canary pods. status: 1/2 canary pods in CrashLoopBackOff, other canaries are Running but not passing readiness.
mike: I see repeated SIGTERM in canary pod logs right after readiness probe success: "Received SIGTERM, shutting down" then later stuck Terminating due to preStop hook. excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z INFO PreStop: starting graceful shutdown
2026-03-15T09:12:33Z WARN Termination exceeded grace period, SIGKILL pending
2026-03-15T09:12:33Z ERR HTTP/1.1 502 bad gateway
```
jade: HPA metrics show CPU spike but desiredReplicas increased, pods pending in Terminating state on node-3. kubectl get pods shows evictions. Possibly node drain interaction?
emma: customer-impact: a handful of high-throughput customers on us-east are seeing 10-20% request failures. Not global but several accounts reporting degraded SLAs.
sara (oncall): initial hypothesis: new image introduced longer shutdown path (preStop) + orchestration/feature flag triggered traffic shift -> burst of evictions -> availability hole.
raj: checking rollout config: strategy has maxUnavailable=10%, surge=0, canary 10%. Feature flag system toggled traffic to canary via releases API around 09:11. I suspect maxUnavailable combined with node eviction caused more pods to go away than expected.
mike: also found HPA minReplicas=0 configured for this deploy config (oops). On traffic spike HPA took time to scale up; combined with pods stuck terminating -> shortage.
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: immediate mitigation options: 1) kill feature-flag to stop traffic to v2.4.0 2) scale deployment manually to desired replicas 3) kubectl drain node-3 --ignore-daemonsets? (risky) 4) rollback to prev revision. See https://runbooks.redwood.local/deployments/canary-failure
sara (oncall): action plan: (1) toggle feature flag kill-switch (2) trigger deploy rollback to v2.3.1 canary abort (3) scale up prev revision to cover customer traffic. raj/mike take 1/2 respectively. jade assist with scaling. I will coordinate comms.
raj: toggling FF now -> POST /flags/cutover kill=true ... response 200. Confirming traffic shift away from canary.
mike: starting rollback: deploy-bot rollback runtime-inference --to-revision=v2.3.1 --force
deploy-bot: Rollback started for runtime-inference -> v2.3.1. Rolling back canary traffic and creating rollout abort.
jade: manually scaling replica set v2.3.1 to 40 -> kubectl scale rs/runtime-inference-v2-3-1 --replicas=40. HPA temporarily disabled.
emma: monitoring: error-rate dropping to 1.2% across us-east, latency normalizing. Affected customers reporting improvement.
sara (oncall): good. keep HPA disabled until we confirm preStop fix and adjust minReplicas. Followups: patch preStop to honor grace period and add readiness-delay on shutdown; set HPA minReplicas=2 in prod and adjust rollout surges.
raj: logging follow-up: collecting core dumps and attaching to ticket #INC-10234. Will open PR to revert preStop change if needed.
mike: closing incident: rollback successful, traffic normalized. re-enable HPA with minReplicas=2 after canary validation window.
sara (oncall): handing off to raj for postmortem and remediation tasks. Please update incident doc with timeline and customer list. tagging @oncall-next. :white_check_mark:
